source_refs.note: Exercise 13.3, Question 2: maximum of S(x) = 100 - 5x^2 and its rate of change (book p.257). Answer key (PDF 311) prints it as number 5.

blocks.prompt: 2. Structural stress on a bridge is modeled by the function \(S(x) = 100 - 5x^2\), where \(x\) is the distance from the center of the bridge. Find the point where the stress is maximum and calculate the rate of change of stress at that point.
blocks.explanation:
A maximum-value question.
We must find where \(S(x)\) is greatest, the maximum stress, and \(S'\) there.
Plan: find \(S'(x)\), set it to 0, check that it is a maximum, then evaluate.
steps:
Given: \(S(x) = 100 - 5x^2\).
To find: the point of maximum stress, the maximum stress, and the rate of change there.
Method: At a highest point of a smooth curve the tangent is horizontal, so \(S'(x) = 0\). We confirm it is a maximum by the sign of \(S'\) on each side.

Differentiate
\[S'(x) = -10x\]
Why: Power rule; the constant 100 gives 0.

Set the derivative to zero
\[-10x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\]
Why: Only at \(x = 0\) is the slope zero.

Confirm a maximum
\[x < 0:\ S'(x) > 0\]
\[x > 0:\ S'(x) < 0\]
Why: The stress increases up to \(x = 0\) and decreases after it. (Also \(-5x^2 \le 0\), so \(S(x) \le 100\) always.)

Maximum stress and rate of change
\[S(0) = 100 - 0 = 100\]
\[S'(0) = -10(0) = 0\]
Why: Substitute \(x = 0\) into \(S\) and \(S'\).
blocks.final_answer: Maximum at \(x = 0\) (the centre of the bridge); maximum stress \(= 100\); rate of change there \(= 0\)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key numbers the answers of Exercise 13.3 as 4, 5, 6, 8, 11, 12, 13, 14 instead of 1 to 8. The answer to this question is printed under number 5: Max. stress \(= 100\), Rate of change \(= 0\), which is correct.
